article.title: Outsourcing War
article.author: John P. Ruehl
article.content: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. The election was a major setback for Trump and the MAGA party. But still, our Republic is in danger. The Project 2025 Christian Nationalist crowd continue to run the administration. And with the appointment of the fanatical Stephen Miller as chief of staff, Trump appears to be doubling down. Moreover, with his suspected cognitive decline, he may pose an even greater threat to the social order that our nation and Western allies have enjoyed for generations. Other powers seek to destroy our Republic. Trump’s best friend Vladimir Putin despises America for its principles and its support of Ukraine’s fight for independence and democracy. And internally, players like Elon Musk and Peter Thiel scorn democratic governance, which they view as inefficient and obsolete. They supported Trump’s autocratic ambitions. Musk alone poured half a billion dollars into the midterm elections backing Republican candidates who blindly support Trump’s goals. Related: Are Billionaire Politicians Becoming the New Normal? Peter Thiel is a Silicon Valley technocrat with a net worth of $37.7 billion . He is not a showman, like Musk, but is as dangerous. Here is his view of government : “I think it is only a small exaggeration to say that the government is so fundamentally evil that to deny the evil nature of the government is equal to denying the existence of the devil… I think it is better for us try to do something noble than to spend the rest of our lives trying to make compromises with the base.” What could be more un-American than the idea that government “of the people, by the people, and for the people” is evil and that compromise, which is the essence of democracy, is less than noble. Thiel, a mentor to JD Vance, fueled Vance’s rapid rise in government. He invested $15 million in Vance’s Ohio senate campaign and arranged Vance’s introduction to Donald Trump at Mar-a-Lago where he smoothed over Vance’s earlier criticism of Trump, which ultimately led to his selection as Vice President. Vance share’s Thiel’s philosophy of government. Thiel and Musk believe government should be run like a corporation, i.e., under a CEO. Rather than an elected president, the CEO would be appointed, ostensibly by a board composed of oligarch technocrats. Both Musk and Thiel advocate stripping away federal regulations and civil service protections, arguing that the state should operate with the lean efficiency and speed of a Silicon Valley startup. This ideology was evident in Musk’s Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), which utilized corporate tactics—like mass workforce reductions and executive orders—to bypass traditional bureaucratic checks and balances. Did Musk’s DOGE enterprise cut costs? No t even close to what Musk claimed it did, and far less than the $2 trillion he initially claimed it would. He wiped out the USAID Agency. And look at the consequences. The Center for Infectious Disease Research at the University of Minnesota estimates that 750,000 lives have been lost and a UCLA Fielding School of Public Health researcher finds that cuts may lead to more than 14 million additional deaths globally by 2030—the Theil-Musk ideology in action. Related: The Business of AI Fear: Who Profits From Doomsday Hype? This simplistic philosophy fails in two essential ways: it lacks values. Good governance requires a moral foundation, not just efficiency. it lacks purpose. A government should exist to serve the common good, not merely to cut costs, especially as Trump claims the US economy is stronger than ever. The effectiveness of a government cannot be measured solely in economic terms. Its performance must be judged against its founding principles. A CEO in charge of government is no different than a dictator. There are few instances in history where a benevolent dictator served to advance the common good. Benign autocrats are rare, and the lack of accountability inherently risks corruption, systemic oppression, and catastrophic failure, making democracy far more resilient, as demonstrated by America’s 250-year history. The Thiel-Musk philosophy is, at best, wildly optimistic in the short term and doomed to failure in the long term. Accountability Musk must be held accountable. His interference with Ukraine’s access to the Starshield military satellite system, operated under his direction, must be investigated. Trump and Musk blame each other for aiding Russia, but a decision with such consequences should never have been made without democratic accountability. Ukraine’s struggle parallels America’s fight for independence in 1776, and so the public overwhelmingly supports Ukraine’s cause. Musk’s DOGE sabotage of USAID, an agency established by Congress, must also be investigated. Created in 1961 by President Kennedy, it was formally codified by Congress as an independent agency in 1998. Can this, or any administration, simply dissolve an agency so established? There are reasons against a third impeachment of Donald Trump. The earlier failed attempts served to divide the nation and drew attention away from other urgent matters that faced congress. And Republican gaslighting made those attempts appear as political revenge. But accountability, justice, and the rule of law are far more important than motivation. Yet pundits are already asking Democratic leaders, will you seek revenge? The question they should be asking is, will you seek justice? Related: Migrants Are Not the Weapon, Governments Are One must consider Trump’s access to America’s most confidential information in the context of his close relationship with Vladimir Putin and his admiration for other autocratic leaders. With his flagrant dishonesty and lack of respect for our Constitution, he simply cannot be trusted to act in the nation’s interest. The danger Trump poses to our national security is real. He should be removed from office. Impeachment appears to be the best solution. Sixty-seven senate votes are necessary. When all the votes are counted, Democrats will likely have fifty-six. There just may be eleven Republicans who care enough about national security to remove him from office. Democrats, a party for the people? There must be consequences for those who violate our Constitution and laws. Democrats have a responsibility to ensure that justice is served. But Democrats need to do more. They must demonstrate that they are for the people. An October Gallup Poll reported that only 43% of U.S. adults view the Democratic Party favorably. And the party must reckon with the fact that Americans chose Trump and his MAGA supporters in two elections. Trump won because people are dissatisfied with the political system the favors wealth and corporations; dissatisfied with the system that shifted eighty trillion dollars from the bottom 90% to the top one percent between 1975 and 2023. On average that is $247,000 for everyone in the bottom 90%, which is 60% greater than their average net worth ($153,000). Unquestionably, American government has favored the wealthy. Democrats and Republicans alike share responsibility. Trump promised change but failed to deliver. To regain the public confidence, Democrats must deliver; make government work for the common good. If they fail to address the sources of public dissatisfaction, resentment and distrust will continue to grow and fester. Changing our economic system so that wealth generated by economic and technical progress benefits the common good rather than the wealthy alone is a monumental task. As AI eliminates both white and blue-collar jobs, the present means of allotting income by salaries and wages and taxing that income will soon become obsolete. Related: America and Russia: Why a 250-Year Rivalry Never Found Its Footing We must find new methods of compensation and taxation that distribute economic gains fairly. Without change, wealth inequality will continue to grow, threatening the stability of our economic system. The current course is unsustainable. The Republican party no longer has the wherewithal to address problems of this nature. Democrats must lead the way.
